tasks.title: Lecture #10
tasks.instruction: Listen to a short talk about Astronomy.
tasks.transcript: In ancient times, many people believed the earth was a flat disc. Well over 2000 years ago, the ancient Greek philosophers were able to put forward two good arguments proving that it was not. Direct observations of heavenly bodies was the basis of both these arguments. First, the Greeks knew that during eclipses of the moon, the earth was between the sun and the moon, and they saw that during these eclipses, the earth’s shadow on the moon was always round. They realized this could be true only if the earth was spherical. If the earth were a flat disc, then its shadow during eclipses would not be a perfect circle, it would be stretched out into a long ellipse. The second argument was based on what the Greeks saw during their travels. They noticed that the North Star, or Polaris, appeared lower in the sky when they traveled south, in more northerly regions, the North Star appeared to them to be much higher in the sky. By the way, it was also from this difference in the apparent position of the North Star that the Greeks first calculated the approximate distance around the circumference of the earth, a figure recorded in ancient documents says 400000 stadia, that's the plural of the word stadium. Today, it’s not known exactly what length one stadium represents, but let’s say it was about 200 meters, the length of many athletic stadiums. This would make the Greek’s estimate about twice the figure accepted today, a very good estimate for those writing so long before even the first telescope was invented.

questions.stem: What is the talk mainly about?

options.A: How ancient philosophers measured the distance between heavenly bodies.
options.B: How ancient philosophers explained the cause of an eclipse of the Moon.
options.C: Why ancient philosophers thought the Earth was a sphere.
options.D: Why ancient philosophers thought the Earth moved around the Sun.

questions.analysis: 答案：C 题目问的是：这段讲话的主要内容是什么？ 定位原文： Well over 2000 years ago, the ancient Greek philosophers were able to put forward two good arguments proving that it was not. Direct observations of heavenly bodies was the basis of both these arguments. 选项分析： A. How ancient philosophers measured the distance between heavenly bodies（古代哲学家如何测量天体之间的距离）。讲话虽提到古希腊人计算了地球周长，但并非主要内容，所以A选项错误。 B. How ancient philosophers explained the cause of an eclipse of the Moon（古代哲学家如何解释月食的成因）。月食只是第一个论据中的现象，并非讲话主题，所以B选项错误。 C. Why ancient philosophers thought the Earth was a sphere（为什么古代哲学家认为地球是球体）。讲话围绕古希腊人提出的两个论据展开，旨在证明地球是球体而非平面，因此C选项正确。 D. Why ancient philosophers thought the Earth moved around the Sun（为什么古代哲学家认为地球围绕太阳运动）。基于讲话未讨论日心说，所以D选项错误。

questions.stem: According to the professor, what were the beliefs of the Greek philosophers based upon?

options.A: How the natural world was described in Greek mythology.
options.C: The writings of philosophers from other societies.

questions.analysis: 答案：B 题目问的是：根据教授的说法，希腊哲学家的观点基于什么？ 定位原文： Direct observations of heavenly bodies was the basis of both these arguments. 选项分析： A. How the natural world was described in Greek mythology（希腊神话对自然界的描述）。由于讲话未提及神话，所以A选项错误。 B. What they observed directly（他们直接观察到的事物）。讲话明确指出直接观察天体是这两个论据的基础，因此B选项正确。 C. The writings of philosophers from other societies（其他社会哲学家的著作）。基于讲话未提及其他社会的著作，所以C选项错误。 D. Measurements made with scientific instruments（用科学仪器进行的测量）。因为古希腊时期尚未发明望远镜等科学仪器，所以D选项错误。

questions.stem: What does the professor say about ancient Greeks who traveled south?

options.A: They noticed an apparent change in the position of the North Star.
options.B: They observed eclipses at different times of the year.
options.C: They were the first to estimate the distance between heavenly bodies.
options.D: They wanted to prove that the Earth was flat.

questions.analysis: 答案：A 题目问的是：教授对向南旅行的古希腊人有什么说法？ 定位原文： They noticed that the North Star, or Polaris, appeared lower in the sky when they traveled south, in more northerly regions, the North Star appeared to them to be much higher in the sky. 选项分析： A. They noticed an apparent change in the position of the North Star（他们注意到北极星的位置发生了明显变化）。讲话明确指出向南旅行时北极星在天空中显得更低，因此A选项正确。 B. They observed eclipses at different times of the year（他们在一年中的不同时间观察月食）。基于讲话未提及月食观察时间，所以B选项错误。 C. They were the first to estimate the distance between heavenly bodies（他们是最早估算天体之间距离的人）。讲话提到的是估算地球周长，而非天体间距离，所以C选项错误。 D. They wanted to prove that the Earth was flat（他们想证明地球是平的）。由于他们观察到北极星位置变化恰恰证明了地球是球体，所以D选项错误。

questions.stem: What does the professor say the term stadium refers to?

options.A: A place for making astronomical observations.
options.B: An instrument used for observing stars.

questions.analysis: 答案：C 题目问的是：教授说“stadium”这个词指的是什么？ 定位原文： a figure recorded in ancient documents says 400000 stadia, that's the plural of the word stadium. Today, it’s not known exactly what length one stadium represents, but let’s say it was about 200 meters, the length of many athletic stadiums. 选项分析： A. A place for making astronomical observations（进行天文观测的地方）。基于讲话中stadium是长度单位，并非地点，所以A选项错误。 B. An instrument used for observing stars（用于观察恒星的仪器）。由于讲话未将其描述为仪器，所以B选项错误。 C. A unit of measurement（一种测量单位）。讲话明确说明stadia是stadium的复数形式，并讨论了一个stadium代表的长度，因此C选项正确。 D. The North Star（北极星）。因为讲话中北极星是Polaris，与stadium无关，所以D选项错误。
